questions.question: Who makes the decision regarding the savings and loan activities in a Self Help Group (SHG)?
questions.solution: A Self Help Group (SHG) is a financial committee of 15-20 people. It is generally based in a village or other economically backward area and is aimed at pooling of resources and extending loans to the members on a case-by-case basis.

questions.question: In Indian constitution, the method of election of President has been taken from which country?
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is __**Ireland**__.

 
 

 
 
__Source__

 
 
 
__Features Borrowed __

 
 
 

 
 
US Constitution

 
 
 
Fundamental rights, independence of the judiciary, judicial review, the impeachment of the president, removal of Supreme Court and high court judges and post of vice-president

 
 
 

 
 
British Constitution

 
 
 
Parliamentary government, Rule of law, legislative procedure, single citizenship, Cabinet system, prerogative writs, parliamentary privileges, and bicameralism.

 
 
 

 __**Irish Constitution**__
 Directive Principles of State Policy, the nomination of members to Rajya Sabha, and __**method of election of the president**__.
 
 

**Extra information:**

 
• The President of India is elected by members of an electoral college instead of direct elections. Following are the members of an electoral college:

 
 
• Elected members of both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• Elected members of state legislative assemblies.
 
• Elected members of legislative assemblies of UTs of Delhi and Puducherry.
 
 
 
• The method adopted for the election of the President is a system of proportional representation by the means single transferable vote.
 
• The voter is required to indicate the preference on the ballot paper and he can mark as many preferences as the number of candidates.
 
• The voting takes place in phases and the candidate securing the least number of first preferences is eliminated in each phase.
 
• The process is carried on and at last, a person securing the required quota of votes stands elected.

questions.question: What is the literal meaning of the term "Quo-Warranto"?
questions.solution:
Option** 3** is correct, i.e. __**By what authority (or) warrant**__.

__
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as; Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• The literal meaning of** Quo-Warranto** is ‘**by what authority**__’. It is one of the five writs that can be issued by the Supreme Court and High Courts to question the authority of the government office that has passed the challenged order.
 
• 
 
 
 

 __Article__
 __Consists of__
 
 

 Article 32
 
 
Right to move the Supreme court for the enforcement of fundamental rights including the writs.

 __
 
• habeas corpus
 
• mandamus
 
• prohibition
 
• certiorari
 
• **quo warranto**
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Habeas Corpus: This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained whether in prison or in private custody, before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
 
• Mandamus: The writ of command is issued by supreme or high court when any government, court, corporation, or any public authority has to do a public duty but fails to do so.
 
• Prohibition: A writ of prohibition is issued by a Court to prohibit the lower courts, tribunals and other quasi-judicial authorities from doing something beyond their authority.
 
• Certiorari: The writ of certiorari can be issued by the supreme or high court for quashing the order already passed by an inferior court, tribunal or quasi-judicial authority.
 
• Quo-Warranto__: The writ of quo-warranto can be issued by the supreme or high court for asking of by what authority or warrant. It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office.

questions.question: Who was given the title of "The Ambassador of Hindu – Muslim Unity" for being the architect and mastermind of the historic Lucknow Pact?
questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct, i.e. __**Muhammad Ali Jinnah**__.

Muhammad Ali Jinnah:

 
• He was a lawyer, politician, and the founder of Pakistan.
 
• Jinnah served as leader of the All - India Muslim League from **1913** until Pakistan's creation on **14 August 1947**.
 
• Muhammed Ali Jinnah was the first Governor-General of Pakistan and is referred to as Qaid-e-Azam.
 
• The Lucknow Pact of **1916** was aimed at getting all the religious factions of the country (moderates, extremists, and the Muslim League) united.

questions.question: What is the name of the court poet of King Harshavardhana?
questions.solution: Banabhatt was the court poet of King Harshvardhana in 7th Century. He wrote the biography of Harshavardhan called Harshacharita and one of the world's earliest novels, Kadambari.

questions.question: Marble comes under which category of rocks?
questions.solution: Marble is a metamorphic rock, made from recrystallized minerals like calcite or dolomite. It is most commonly used for making sculptures and buildings.

questions.concept: Geography (World Geography), Science Technology and Inventions
questions.question: Which of the following is most important for absorption of heat radiated from the Sun as well as from the Earth?
questions.solution: Molecules of carbon dioxide (CO₂) can absorb heat energy from infrared (IR) radiation. This ability to absorb and re - emit infrared energy is what makes CO₂ an effective heat - trapping greenhouse gas.

questions.question: Which among the following has segmented body?
questions.solution: Phylum Annelida is the category of worms and includes any and every worm like earthworm, rag worm, leeches etc. These worms are invertebrates and have different segments in one body.

questions.question: Synapse gap is present between which of the following?
questions.solution: Synapse is a structure in the human nervous system that allows the passage of the chemical or electrical signal from one neuron (nerve cell) to other neuron.

questions.question: Which organ has ﬁnger like outgrowths which are called as Villi (Singular Villus)?
questions.solution: Villi present in the small intestine are small finger - like tissue projections which increase the surface area of the intestine and contain specialized cells that transport substances into the bloodstream.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
questions.solution: Electric current, despite of having magnitude and direction, is not considered as a vector quantity because it doesn’t always obey the Laws of vector addition, which a vector necessarily follows.

questions.question: The phenomena of raising the outer edge of the curved roads above the inner edge to provide necessary centripetal force to the vehicles to take a safe turn is called _____.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__

Banking of road: The phenomenon of raising the outer edge of the curved road compared to its inner edge is called the banking of the road.

• In the level curve of circular motion, the maximum velocity without skidding depends on μs i.e. frictional force between tyre and road.
 
• But friction is not always a reliable source for providing the required centripetal force for the vehicle.
 
• Due to various factors like rain, type of tyre and many others.
 
• Therefore, banking of road helps the vehicle to overcome this.

questions.question: C++ is ________.
questions.solution: C++ is an object oriented programming language. It comes under the category of ‘general - purpose programming language’ that is used for writing software in different variety of application domains.

questions.question: What are isobars?

options.text: Elements with same atomic number but different mass number
Elements with different atomic number but same mass number
Elements with different atomic number and different mass number
Elements with same atomic number and same mass number

questions.solution: Isobars are atoms of different chemical elements that have different atomic number but same mass number. This is because they have same number of nucleons.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT?

I. Haematite : Iron

II. Pitchblende : Copper

III. Monazite : Thorium
questions.solution: Haematite and Monazite are the ores of iron and thorium respectively whereas, pitchblende (also called Uraninite) is the ore of Uranium and not copper.

questions.solution:

questions.question: The 7th pay commission has retained the rate of annual increment of _____.
questions.solution: The rate of annual increment is being retained by the 7th Pay Commission of Indian. This rate was last modified in the 6th Pay Commission when it was set at 3%.

questions.question: Who discovered malaria causing germs?
questions.solution: Charles Louis Alphonse Laveran was the first person to discover the causative agents of malaria. He was also awarded Nobel Prize in Medicine or physiology in 1907 for his discovery.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book titled 'The Gita for Children'?
questions.solution: ‘The Gita for Children’ is the book written by Roopa Pai which was released in 2015. It is aimed at spreading the teachings of Indian text Bhagwat Gita to children in a lucid manner.

questions.question: With which country India celebrated its 25th year of diplomatic ties in 2017?
questions.solution: India and Israel had held a series of events in February 2017 to celebrate 25 years of establishment of their diplomatic ties. India had established full diplomatic relationship with Israel in 1992 and had recognised the country in 1950.

questions.question: Which Asian country has opened 'Duge Bridge' (world's highest road bridge) for use in year 2016?
questions.solution: Duge Bridge is a cable bridge near Liupanshui city in China. It was opened for use in 2016 is the highest in the world with the road deck sitting over 565 metres above the Beipan River.
